add.text: In the Late Devonian another group of progymnosperms gave rise to Archaeopteris, the first really large trees known.
The stratigraphically oldest known progymnosperms belong to the Middle Devonian order Aneurophytales, with forms such as Protopteridium whose vegetative organs were relatively loose clusters of axes.
Chilenia was an ancient microcontinent or terrane that affected many of the older rocks of central Chile and western Argentina.
Another source dates Chilenia's accretion to Cuyania, from which it had been separated by oceanic crust, to about 420–390 million years ago, when Cuyania was already joined to Gondwana.
Microbial reefs dominated under the warmer conditions of the early and late Devonian, while coral-stromatoporoid reefs dominated during the cooler middle Devonian.

The Devonian has been wrongly characterised as a greenhouse age because of sampling bias: most early Devonian discoveries came from western Europe and eastern North America, which then straddled the Equator.
As plants took hold on the continental margins, oxygen levels increased and carbon dioxide dropped, although much less dramatically.
For eroded or buried craters, the stated diameter usually refers to an estimate of the original rim diameter and may not match present surface features.
The Ilyinets crater is an impact crater in Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine.
It lies at the boundary of the Ros–Tikych and Dniester–Bug megastructures of the Ukrainian Shield.
Cladoselache lived in the Late Devonian (Famennian) of North America and is one of the best-known early cartilaginous fish (Chondrichthyes).
Cladoselache had cladodont teeth, with a large sharp central cusp surrounded by one or two pairs of smaller cusps.
Cladoselache is often called the earliest shark in broad ecological terms, though it is only distantly related to modern sharks.
Notostracans are 2–5 centimetres long, with a broad carapace at the front and a long, slender abdomen.
Notostracans are omnivores living on the bottom of temporary pools and shallow lakes.
The Woodleigh event was thought in the early 2000s to date between 259 and 201 million years ago, but is now thought to date from 364 ± 8 million years ago.
Woodleigh's central uplift, interpreted as 20 kilometres in diameter, was first intersected by drilling in the late 1970s, but its significance as an impact structure was only realised in 1997.
Woodleigh, Acraman and Tookoonooka are the three largest of the two dozen or more known impact structures in Australia.
The Warburton craters formed when an asteroid or comet split into two main pieces and hit the Australian continent, then part of Gondwana.
The East Warburton crater is adjacent to the West Warburton crater, which is also around 200 km in diameter.
Chitinozoans are flask-shaped, organic-walled marine microfossils produced by an as yet unknown organism.
The flask-shaped chitinozoans completely died out during the Hangenberg Event.
Bambach (2006) estimated that 31% of marine genera died out in the last substage of the Famennian.
A 2024 study found little support for Gastornithiformes and placed Gastornis in the Galliformes crown group, closer to Phasianoidea than to megapodes.
No fossil of Gastornis has been found younger than about 45 million years.
Plant fossils, especially seeds and fruits, are abundant in the London Clay and have been collected for almost 300 years.
The London Clay is a stiff bluish clay that becomes brown when weathered and oxidized.
Another source gives Eocene Thermal Maximum 3 as about 52.5 million years ago, after ETM2 at about 53.2 million years ago.
The Cambay amber was being deposited at the peak of the Early Eocene Climatic Optimum.
India was colliding with Asia at this time, acting as a biotic ferry, so the amber may help show the biotic interchange between the two landmasses.
Mayflies have also been found in the Cambay amber.
The Sevier orogeny affected western North America from northern Canada to Mexico.
The Sevier orogeny was preceded by the Nevadan, Sonoman and Antler orogenies and partially overlapped in time and space with the Laramide orogeny.
Monte Bolca is rich in fish, with 250 species in 140 genera, 90 families and 19 orders.
Monte Bolca has the most diverse fish fauna of any Cenozoic fossil site, with many of the earliest fossil occurrences of modern marine fish groups.
The European Cenozoic Rift System is a 1,100 km long system of rifts formed in the foreland of the Alps as the lithosphere responded to the Alpine and Pyrenean orogenies.
The system began to form in the Late Eocene, and parts, especially the Upper and Lower Rhine Grabens, remain seismically active and cause most of the larger earthquakes in Europe north of the Alps.
Volcanic activity accompanied, and in some places preceded, the rift system's development over large parts of it and persisted into the Quaternary.
The middle Eocene shifted to a cooler climate at the end of the Early Eocene Climatic Optimum, around 47.8 Ma, briefly interrupted by the Middle Eocene Climatic Optimum.
The Eocene held the warmest period of the Cenozoic and also marked the decline into an icehouse climate and the rapid expansion of the Antarctic ice sheet.
Another source says nearly all the Kula Plate had been subducted beneath the North American Plate by about 40 million years ago.
The Geiseltal fossils, especially the vertebrates and mammals, are uniquely preserved in lignite, which is found nowhere else in Central Europe.
The Geiseltal lignite is divided into four main seams, of which the lower three were mainly fossil-bearing.
The Kishenehn Formation is a Paleogene stratigraphic unit in Montana.
The first phosphate deposits in Quercy were discovered in 1869 and published independently by Daubré and Trutat in 1871.
Nearly all Quercy fly pupae were preserved as isolated endocasts, many still covered by the puparium, the hardened skin of the last larval instar.
The fusion happened when the mid-ocean ridge in the Indian Ocean that separated the two plates ceased spreading.
Along the northern Ninety East Ridge there appears to be a weakness zone where the Indian and Australian plates are going different ways.
Differential movement has compressed the plate near its centre at Sumatra, with a possible division into separate Indian and Australian plates again.
The Logoisk crater was found by accident during routine exploration drilling near the village of Kuzevichi in the 1970s.
Drilling found Quaternary deposits to 160 m, then 230 m of layered clays and lacustrine sediments, then 240 m of breccias.
It was suggested that the crater may contain impact diamonds, but this has not been confirmed.
There have been at least 183 geomagnetic reversals over the last 83 million years, on average once every 450,000 years or so.
The rate of reversals in the Earth's magnetic field has varied widely over time.
Remnants of the Eridanos are found across northern Europe, from the North Sea and the Netherlands in the west to sediments in northern Lapland.
Neogene uplift of the South Swedish Dome deflected the Eridanos from its path across south-central Sweden to a course south of Sweden in the Pliocene.
After the Eridanos disappeared, the Rhine became the most important river in this part of the North Sea Basin.
When rifting reached the Tanzanian Craton, the rift split into the eastern Gregory Rift and the western Albertine Rift, separated by the 1,300 kilometres wide East African Plateau.
The rift is widest at its northern end in the Afar region, narrowing to a few kilometers in northern Tanzania.
Lake Wanapitei is an impact crater lake within the city of Greater Sudbury, Ontario, Canada.
It lies next to the nearby but unrelated Sudbury impact crater and is one of the world's largest lakes entirely within a single municipality.
The Cascade Arc includes nearly 20 major volcanoes among over 4,000 separate volcanic vents.
In the North Cascades geologists have not identified with certainty any volcanic rocks as old as 35 million years.
Mistastin Lake was first identified as a possible impact crater in 1968, after being viewed from space.
Cubic zirconia around the crater rim suggests the impact generated temperatures above 2,370 °C, roughly 43% of the temperature of the Sun's surface.
Mistastin crater is in northwestern inland Labrador, due west of Natuashish, near Quebec.

The Ring of Fire does not extend across the southern Pacific from New Zealand to the Antarctic Peninsula or the southern tip of South America, because plate boundaries there are divergent instead of convergent.
The southwest Ring of Fire is more complex, with smaller plates colliding with the Pacific plate at the Mariana Islands, the Philippines, eastern Indonesia, Papua New Guinea, Tonga and New Zealand.
As diatoms fell to the lake bottom, plants and animals that had recently died were preserved by the diatom falls.
Fossil plants, especially their leaves, have been the most useful source of information on paleoclimate during deposition of the Florissant Formation.
